claims.text: The eutectic high-entropy alloy has a well-developed, self-passivating oxide film.
The constituent phases have locally different electrochemical potentials.
The constituent phases have different mechanical hardnesses.
Elevated temperature diminishes the stability of the passive oxide film.
Phase boundaries concentrate mechanical stress because of differences between the constituent phases.
Phase boundaries facilitate localized passive-film breakdown.
Sliding wear preferentially removes or disrupts the thermally weakened oxide film at phase boundaries.
Disruption of the oxide film exposes fresh, chemically active substrate.
The exposed sites behave as vulnerable anodic regions.
Exposure of the anodic sites accelerates localized corrosion at phase boundaries.
Interfacial corrosion softens the microstructure.
Corrosion-induced softening increases subsequent mechanical wear.
Mechanical removal of protective material and corrosion of exposed material form a positive feedback cycle.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion produce total material loss greater than the sum of losses from wear-only and corrosion-only exposures.
Simultaneous exposure produces greater wear-track volume than the wear-only control.
Simultaneous exposure produces deeper corrosion pits at phase boundaries than the corrosion-only control.
Chloride must be present at a sufficient concentration for exposed metal to undergo the proposed localized attack.
Mechanical loading must generate sufficient localized abrasion at phase boundaries for the proposed feedback mechanism to operate.
A simultaneous wear-corrosion test, a wear-only control, and a corrosion-only control can distinguish synergistic degradation from additive degradation.
The proposed mechanism is falsified if combined degradation is not super-additive or if the passive film remains intact at phase boundaries.

contradictions.description: The baseline describes wear-only testing under identical chemical conditions with minimal corrosion, whereas the falsification design places the wear-only samples in an inert electrolyte. These are materially different chemical conditions.
